headline: Android 17 Continuity Feature Finally Arrives, Mimicking Apple's Handoff
summary: Android 17 introduces 'Continue On,' a feature designed to seamlessly transfer tasks between devices, ending the need for workarounds like emailing yourself drafts.
details: Android 17 is set to launch with a new feature called 'Continue On,' which aims to bridge the gap in cross-device continuity that has long separated Android from Apple's ecosystem.

This new functionality allows users to start a task on their phone, such as writing an email in Gmail or working on a document in Google Docs, and then seamlessly pick up exactly where they left off on a tablet or other connected device.
Previously, users often resorted to emailing themselves drafts or using cloud storage as a workaround for transferring unfinished tasks between devices. 'Continue On' aims to eliminate this friction.
The feature functions similarly to Apple's Handoff. When a task is initiated on one device, it appears as a one-tap suggestion on the taskbar of a connected device, allowing for instant continuation.

Initial tests show 'Continue On' working effectively with core Google apps like Gmail, Google Docs, and Chrome. For instance, a Gmail draft started on a phone can be resumed on a tablet, and a Chrome browsing session can be transferred.

To enable 'Continue On,' users need to navigate to Settings > Connected devices > Connection preferences > Cross-device services > Continue activity and enable 'Tasks.' The feature requires the same Google account to be signed in on both devices.

While 'Continue On' offers a significant improvement for Google's native apps, its full potential will be realized as developers implement Google's handoff APIs to make their third-party applications compatible with the feature.
